commands.review_summary:
Adds digest-addressed cloud review snapshots with stage-only publication and later cutover, authenticated contract checks, sanitized SQLite upload/readback, expanded hydration coverage, and supporting tests and documentation.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level: return a complete publisher candidate in `Snapshot` while `ActiveSnapshotID` remains the prior serving digest, a state explicitly modeled by crawlkit v0.14.1; the matcher returns false.
commands.review_followup: - The merge blocker is a narrow mechanical mismatch between the pinned dependency contract and one candidate-matching condition plus its fixtures.

target.title: feat(cloud): publish content-addressed review snapshots
target.body:
## Summary

- publish complete Gitcrawl cloud-v2 snapshots from one exact source SQLite digest
- stage snapshots without reader cutover when requested, then resume and cut over the same immutable snapshot later
- preserve default reader cutover for existing publish callers
- normalize `source_sync_at` and per-dataset freshness maxima by parsed RFC3339 instants, then emit canonical UTC timestamps
- validate the complete writer and reader contract before mutation while accepting additive optional remote query arguments
- call the advertised authenticated `/v1/whoami` route before remote mutation and require the supplied token to hold both publisher and reader roles
- require the advertised reader `GET /sqlite` route for cutover, then verify its required digest header, exact uploaded-manifest source size, byte boundary, and SHA-256
- preserve exact digest, source-sync, schema, publication-profile, generation, and top-level/nested coverage checks after cutover
- hydrate pull-request files, observation-order metadata, coverage, and immutable snapshot provenance
- scrub private source metadata before publication and pin crawlkit v0.14.1

## Safety

- snapshot IDs equal the lowercase SHA-256 of the source SQLite image
- publisher-only tokens fail authenticated preflight before upload, ingest, or cutover mutation
- staged resume requires the exact snapshot capability set, source digest, schema, generation timestamp, and matching complete top-level and nested coverage
- malformed, stale, partial, or reader-incompatible remote contracts fail before publication or cutover
- post-cutover hydration rejects missing or wrong digest/length metadata, truncated bodies, oversized bodies, and body digest mismatch
- post-cutover verification re-reads publisher status and rejects any digest, profile, generation, or coverage drift before hashing the downloaded SQLite body
- the final reader cutover remains gated on crawl-remote snapshot-provenance support

## Validation

- exact head: `90bb68359d01ec1312597d94801773440d7b49b1`
- `gofmt` on all touched Go files
- focused publisher-only/no-mutation, hydration framing/digest, staged-resume coverage, contract, and end-to-end cloud publication tests passed
- `go test ./... -count=1`
- `go vet ./...`
- `git diff --check`
- coordinated against crawl-remote PR https://github.com/openclaw/crawl-remote/pull/36 exact head `f209a73a40c6991d0864dc689304abe808aadc95`
- that remote contract advertises reader-authenticated `GET /sqlite`; its isolated Workerd/R2 proof reports an HTTP 200 SQLite response whose downloaded bytes match the active source digest
- Gitcrawl now rejects the prior `snapshot_bundle_required` post-cutover behavior instead of declaring publication success
